backendLogReconciliation.interpretation: Within the audit window the backend logged 12 notification requests, all HTTP 200. The first pass has no per-request trace, so these aggregate entries cannot uniquely identify the timed-out client request or distinguish Hosting, network and local-client causes. One client transport failure remains disclosed; no backend 15-second database delay was observed in these logs.

cloudReadAfterDeployment.authMetadata: Two ordinary sign-ins can update last-login metadata. The runner changed no application data, accounts, privileges or quota limits.

beforeOneReservationPermitPerDomain.cause: Each Domain allowed two reservation transactions. Four transactions competed on the exact global quota counter; pending callers reached the unchanged 20-second admission deadline. The 40 service_busy responses did not reserve quota.

remainingScope: The cloud baseline used one existing owner and up to eight read clients. Independent-user cloud write capacity is not established by that measurement.
Emulators do not reproduce all production latency, index, transaction contention, quota or autoscaling behavior.
Resource measurements include the load driver and fixture data in the HTTP server process; they are not standalone Cloud Run memory capacity measurements.
Native model throughput, long AI queues and full public traffic have not been stress tested. Daily quota limits are budget bounds, not response-time guarantees.

The deployed read check observed one client transport timeout among 180 load GET requests. Aggregate backend notification logs were HTTP 200, but the first pass lacked per-request traces; the failing network layer is unresolved. The failed receipt remains retained.

newScenario: Intentionally hold first notification GET silently.
